title: Canned Pumpkin 425g

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One-day closure in 7-day week; historical impact estimates ~14% sales reduction; no other evidence of closure impact on this product

adjustment.analysis: The store closure on Monday (2026-10-19) removes one day of sales, reducing the week's potential volume. Based on historical patterns, a full-day closure in a 7-day week reduces sales by ~14% (1/7). No promotions, price changes, or holidays are active. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends and recent sales. The classical uplift model's 1.00 multiplier is correct for Halloween (no effect), and past promotions show no current lift. The closure is the only driver, with moderate evidence from past closures. No other events or price changes justify a change.

  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 17.1 | 5%-95%: 2.9 - 39.1 | 10%-90%: 9.5 - 29.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-65% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
